name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,458

clue.text: Team leader set off with item that's struck in sporting fixture

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
something set off is jolted out of place, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a match is struck to light it; with simply joins it on

explanation.surface: A captain sets off carrying something that gets hit during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The item struck sounds like a ball, but it is the thing you strike to make a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game, a major sporting event between national teams.

clue.text: Second knight leaving cards won by earl

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the knight's letter goes out of the cards won

blocks.note: a trick is the set of cards won in one round of a card game
K is the abbreviation for knight, the one that leaves

explanation.surface: A knight quits the card table while a nobleman scoops the winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Second looks like it describes the knight, but it is the definition, as in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in an instant, so the word names a very brief moment of time, like a second.

clue.text: Bird box controversy

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
a row is a heated dispute

explanation.surface: A bird box causes an argument between neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird box reads as a nesting box, but box is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small, common brown songbird found around houses and gardens.

clue.text: Take up space adjoining one American state

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top
adjoining means sitting right next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
the Roman numeral for one; adjoining joins it on
AM is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An instruction to occupy room next to a single American province.
explanation.walkthrough: American state looks like the whole definition, but American supplies letters and only state defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the fifty United States, in the far north-east of New England.

clue.text: Politician interrupting real time broadcast

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

explanation.surface: A politician cuts into a live, real-time broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician looks like the obvious American one, but it is just the two-letter MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet news is to proclaim it loudly far and wide, much as one would announce it publicly.

clue.text: Various deaths marked by single memorial

indicators.note: various suggests a different, varied arrangement of the next word's letters

explanation.surface: Several deaths are commemorated by one monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone set at the head of a grave serves as a memorial to the person buried there.

clue.text: Trifle with buffet

explanation.surface: A trifle served at a buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle and buffet both suggest food, but trifle means a tiny amount and buffet is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest particle or jot, as in not a whit, so it is a tiny amount.

clue.text: Get rid of small uncertainty without Britain

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is left out of the uncertainty

blocks.note: B abbreviates Britain; this is removed

explanation.surface: Eliminate a little hesitation outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed out is to remove the unwanted elements, as a gardener pulls weeds from a bed.

clue.text: App popular with animals?

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer, the first animal
a ram is a male sheep, the second animal

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: is there a phone app that animals love?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that animals gives two creatures, not a general fondness for pets on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Instagram is a popular photo-sharing social media application for phones.

clue.text: Sweet setter following male wearing new suit

indicators.note: following places the setter's letter after the male's
to be wearing is to be inside clothing, so these letters sit inside the other
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of the word after it

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A dessert-loving compiler trails a man in a fresh suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter is the crossword compiler, giving I; the rearranged suit wraps around the male and the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone cream.

clue.text: Reluctant saver forged stub of cheque

indicators.note: a forged thing is made falsely, so the word before it is remade in a new order
a stub is the stump left at the end, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A cautious saver is reluctant, having faked a cheque stub.
explanation.walkthrough: A cheque stub is the counterfoil you keep, but here stub means the tail end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or unwilling, so it is a synonym of disinclined.

clue.text: Qualification held by roadside greengrocer

indicators.note: held by says the letters are gripped within the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the end of roadside and the start of greengrocer

explanation.surface: A diploma is owned by a fruit seller with a stall at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A university degree is an academic award that qualifies its holder.

clue.text: Finished vocal work depicting country life

explanation.surface: A completed choral piece portraying rural life.
explanation.walkthrough: Vocal work reads as a song, but vocal is the wordplay and work begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral is a poem, painting or piece of music idealising rustic shepherd life.

clue.text: Councillor has headgear

blocks.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor

explanation.surface: A local councillor sports a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowns are royal ceremonial headwear worn by monarchs, a kind of headdress.

clue.text: Soldiers participating in new and free opportunities to vote

indicators.note: new signals that the combined letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Troops take part in fresh and fair elections.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers join the letters of and free before all are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public ballots on a single question, letting the whole electorate decide by vote.

clue.text: Helper of devil eating up one animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the devil eats, taking the other letters inside it

explanation.surface: A devil's assistant gobbling down a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Helper of devil reads as an imp, but of is a link and the devil is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable of the Good Samaritan, the word means anyone who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Rocks placed round river's extremities?

indicators.note: being placed round something means enclosing it

blocks.note: rocks as a verb: sways unsteadily

explanation.surface: Boulders arranged around the ends of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that extremities is a whimsical definition: pigs' feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotters are pigs' feet, the extremities at the ends of a pig's legs, also cooked as food.

clue.text: Frequently archaic old newspapers

explanation.surface: Stale old newspapers are often outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: Archaic belongs to the definition, flagging an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofttimes is an old literary word for often, meaning many times or repeatedly.

clue.text: Theologian left to tuck into rank fish

indicators.note: to tuck into is to be pushed inside, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: a tier is a rank or level

explanation.surface: A churchman leaves to eat some foul-smelling fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck into suggests eating and rank suggests a bad smell; rank is really a row or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is British slang for a very small fish, such as a minnow caught by children.

clue.text: Band trained to go in to drop flood defence

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new form, so the word's letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go inside the word for dropping

blocks.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: A rehearsed band is sent in to lower a barrier against floods.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandbags are sacks filled with sand piled up as a barrier against rising floodwater.

clue.text: Three excited about good puzzle

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the referenced word's letters are jumbled
about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the next letter

blocks.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 3-down

explanation.surface: Three people get worked up over a good brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: Three is not a number here: it points to the answer at 3-down, a common cross-referencing device.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery that is hard to understand or solve.

clue.text: Dishonorable women leaving joint with new soldier stood up

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for women goes out of the joint
in a down clue, standing up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: the elbow is an arm joint
W abbreviates women; this is removed
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: Shameful women walk out of a pub with a new recruit who was jilted.
explanation.walkthrough: Stood up suggests a missed date, but in a down answer it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means base or lacking honour, the opposite of noble in character.

clue.text: Government clear press network

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: The government frees up a press network.
explanation.walkthrough: Press network sounds like the media, but press is the laundry kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a framework or grid of parallel bars, a network of lines or tracks.

clue.text: Engineer in a car plant

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, reshaping the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mechanic sits in a car at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a car factory, but it is a flowering herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a yellow-flowered mountain herb of the daisy family, used in bruise remedies.

clue.text: Dressing is perfect with stems of broccoli

indicators.note: a stem is the lower end of the vegetable, so the tail letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit read as the letter I
the last three letters of broccoli

explanation.surface: A salad dressing is ideal alongside broccoli stalks.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning top quality, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence, served as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: Mud left in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for a vehicle

blocks.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Dirt left behind inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Clart is a Scottish and northern English dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clart is a Scottish and northern English dialect word for sticky dirt or muck.

clue.text: Bank letterheads featuring ornamental band

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the letters are contained within the words before it

blocks.note: found across the end of bank and start of letterheads

explanation.surface: Bank stationery printed with a decorative border.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a decorative chain or ring worn around the ankle, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Books about conflict put away for bully

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the books go round the conflict

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for book, doubled for books
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Books about war are shelved, ready for a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Put away sounds like shelving the books, but it means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat someone is to intimidate them with threats or stern words, as a bully does.

clue.text: Standard river fish

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: An ordinary freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon or trout in its early freshwater stage, marked with dark bars.

clue.text: Careless fellow following German during line dancing

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters of the word before it around
during means within the span of, so the letter sits inside the jumbled word
following places the fellow after the rest

blocks.note: a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A sloppy man trails a German during a line dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, so it describes someone heedless or slack.
